notes: Authoritative SG tort case index used to enrich prompt overlays and support citation grounding in the refine loop. Headnotes are short paraphrases authored for this repository; full text is not redistributed.

authorities.citation: Spandeck Engineering (S) Pte Ltd v Defence Science & Technology Agency [2007] SGCA 37
authorities.headnote: Two-stage test for duty of care in Singapore: threshold factual foreseeability, then proximity, then policy considerations. Universal framework applied across novel duty categories, including pure economic loss.

authorities.citation: Anwar Patrick Adrian v Ng Chong & Hue LLC [2014] SGCA 34
authorities.headnote: Solicitor's duty of care to third parties not in a contractual relationship; application of the Spandeck framework to professional negligence contexts.

authorities.citation: Hii Chii Kok v Ooi Peng Jin London Lucien [2017] SGCA 38
authorities.headnote: Modified Montgomery test for medical advice; departs from pure Bolam. Standard of care differs between diagnosis/treatment (Bolam-Bolitho) and advice (patient-centred).

authorities.citation: See Toh Siew Kee v Ho Ah Lam Ferrocement (Pte) Ltd [2013] SGCA 29
authorities.headnote: Rejection of tripartite visitor classification (invitee/licensee/trespasser) in Singapore; occupiers' liability subsumed under general negligence framework using the Spandeck two-stage test.

authorities.citation: Ng Huat Seng v Munib Mohammad Madni [2017] SGCA 58
authorities.headnote: Two-stage test for vicarious liability: (1) relationship akin to employment, (2) close connection between wrongful act and that relationship. Independent contractors generally excluded absent non-delegable duty.

authorities.citation: Review Publishing Co Ltd v Lee Hsien Loong [2010] SGCA 1
authorities.headnote: Defamation elements in Singapore: (1) statement is defamatory, (2) refers to plaintiff, (3) published. Reynolds public interest defence not adopted; qualified privilege framework applied.

authorities.citation: Ngiam Kong Seng v Lim Chiew Hock [2008] SGCA 23
authorities.headnote: Psychiatric harm claims in Singapore: proximity in relationship, proximity in time/space, and means of perception all considered under the Spandeck framework rather than as rigid Alcock control mechanisms.

authorities.citation: RSP Architects Planners & Engineers v Ocean Front Pte Ltd [1996] 1 SLR(R) 113
authorities.headnote: Pure economic loss recovery for defective buildings; management corporation may recover from architects for latent building defects. Basis for wider Singapore willingness to permit pure economic loss claims.

authorities.citation: Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken AB v Asia Pacific Breweries (Singapore) Pte Ltd [2011] SGCA 22
authorities.headnote: Vicarious liability requires close connection test; frolic-of-employee doctrine applied where employee acts wholly for personal ends.

authorities.citation: Ochroid Trading Ltd v Chua Siok Lui [2018] SGCA 5
authorities.headnote: Illegality defence in Singapore: range-of-factors approach (following Patel v Mirza [2016] UKSC 42) applied to tort and unjust enrichment; retreats from strict reliance/inextricable-link tests.

authorities.citation: Lo Kok Jong v Eng Beng [2024] 1 SLR 964
authorities.headnote: Professional retained by buyer may also owe a duty of care to seller where there is commonality of interest, foreseeability, and proximity, and no policy reasons to negate the duty.
Recent SG High Court application of Spandeck framework to a construction negligence dispute; causation and remoteness analysis follows Wagon Mound (No 1) foreseeability-of-damage-type test.
Neighbour principle: reasonable care owed to persons closely and directly affected by one's acts. Foundational authority for modern negligence and product liability in Singapore.

authorities.citation: Overseas Tankship (UK) Ltd v Morts Dock & Engineering (The Wagon Mound No 1) [1961] AC 388
authorities.headnote: Damage must be of a foreseeable type; egg-shell skull rule refines this for personal injury. Applied in Singapore alongside directness limits.
Strict liability for escape of a dangerous thing accumulated on land through a non-natural use. Applied in Singapore as a discrete tort separate from negligence and nuisance.

statutes.notes: Consolidates civil-law reforms including contributory negligence apportionment.

statutes.citation: Contributory Negligence and Personal Injuries Act (Cap. 54)
statutes.notes: Enables apportionment of damages between claimant and defendant on the basis of comparative fault.
Statutory defences (justification, fair comment, qualified privilege) and remedies for defamation.
Six-year limitation period for tort claims generally; three years for personal injury.
Statutory tort of harassment: threatening/abusive/insulting words or behaviour causing alarm or distress.
Duty of care of employers and occupiers of workplaces; foundation of most SG employer-liability claims.
No-fault compensation scheme; interacts with common-law negligence claims via election provisions.
